title: SCA Minhag of the Week 203: “Tefilat HaDerekh; The Traveler’s Prayer"

chapters.title: Gemara Berakhot Chapter 4 on Tefilat HaDerekh
chapters.about: Rav Chasda, Abaye, singular versus plural wording

chapters.title: Rambam, Beit Yosef, and Shulhan Arukh

summary: Mr. Arking examines the sources and textual variations of Tefilat HaDerekh, comparing Masekhet Berakhot, Rambam, Beit Yosef, and Shulhan Arukh. He discusses differences between reciting the traveler's prayer in the singular versus the plural and whether to include a blessing at the end with Hashem's name. He also explores how Mahzor Aram Soba, Siddur Bet Obed, and the community of Halab approached this prayer.
questions: Should Tefilat HaDerekh be recited in the singular or plural?
How do Masekhet Berakhot chapter 4 and chapter 9 differ regarding the traveler's prayer?
Why did Rambam omit the final blessing from Tefilat HaDerekh?
What was the custom in Halab regarding saying Hashem's name at the end of Tefilat HaDerekh?
How does the text of Tefilat HaDerekh in Siddur Bet Obed compare to its printed Halakha?
